title: Establishing when and how sustained plate tectonics began

concept.text: The innovation would be a convincing reconstruction of when and how Earth developed a persistent, globally connected system of moving tectonic plates. It would distinguish evidence of local subduction-like activity, crustal recycling or mobile regions from evidence that these processes formed an enduring global network. Finding an early example of tectonic activity would therefore be one piece of the reconstruction, rather than sufficient evidence of the full transition.

Conceptual synthesis: the target is both historical and mechanistic—establishing the timing of the transition and explaining the physical conditions that made sustained plate motion possible. A successful reconstruction could identify a prolonged, geographically uneven transition rather than a single first date. It could use younger rocks as well as Hadean material, because evidence of persistence and global connectivity may come from a different interval than the earliest evidence of local activity.

significance.text: Significance assessment: resolving this transition would provide a fundamental account of how Earth's surface and interior became coupled through sustained plate motion. Establishing the timing and mechanism together could explain a major change in how the planet exchanges material and heat, while helping distinguish competing accounts of its geological development. This is the anticipated importance of the proposed achievement; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate that the reconstruction has been accomplished.

Conditional consequences: a well-supported tectonic history could constrain models of continental growth and long-term geochemical cycles by specifying when sustained recycling and plate interactions became available as explanatory mechanisms. Implications for the history of life or the behavior of other planets would require additional evidence and modeling. Establishing Earth's transition would not, by itself, establish a universal planetary sequence or a particular biological consequence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is to infer an enduring global tectonic regime from observations that are geographically scattered and potentially compatible with several histories. A local recycling signal might indicate isolated or intermittent activity without establishing a connected plate network. The reconstruction must therefore explain how individual observations constrain spatial connectivity, duration and the physical mechanism of sustained motion.

Research-framed barriers, not verified findings from the retained source: the supplied research identifies the scarcity of ancient rocks and alteration of potentially diagnostic signatures as major obstacles. Addressing these concerns would require reliable dating, checks that the relevant signatures survived later geological changes, and evidence that the proposed tectonic interpretation fits better than alternatives. The possibility of a gradual or regionally uneven transition must remain open; it is a hypothesis to evaluate rather than an established history in this record.

Proposed engineering and scientific requirement: physical models must connect plausible early-Earth conditions to the initiation and persistence of plate motion, while producing consequences that can be compared with geological observations. Matching one regional signal would be insufficient if the same model could not account for the broader distribution and timing of evidence. Conversely, an apparent mismatch must be assessed against the incompleteness and preservation limits of the geological archive.

current_state.text: The supplied research lists a 2026 study attributed to Valley, Blum, Kitajima and colleagues, titled “Contemporaneous mobile- and stagnant-lid tectonics on the Hadean Earth,” with DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-10066-2. The research reports that its abstract interprets zircon evidence as indicating contrasting tectonic histories in different regions. This makes the study potentially relevant to the distinction between regional mobility and a uniform global regime, but that scientific interpretation could not be independently checked in the supplied review.

The access records differ in a consequential way: the research says the abstract was inspected and full-text access failed, whereas the review found that the retained HTML contained only a cookie challenge. The retained material therefore did not allow the reviewer to verify article identity from its content, examine the abstract, or assess methods, results and limitations. The source index's saved and verified indicators do not resolve that absence of scientific content. This limits what can be concluded here; it is not evidence that the reported study or interpretation is false.

Assessment of the supplied evidence: no verified demonstration in this record establishes the onset date or mechanism of a sustained global plate network. Even if the reported regional zircon interpretation is confirmed, an additional argument would be needed to connect regional tectonic differences to global connectivity and long-term persistence. The review also reports an empty freshness-search record, so the supplied material cannot establish a comprehensive state of knowledge through its stated November 1, 2026 cutoff.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing demonstration: assemble independently dated evidence from multiple regions, explain which observations diagnose local mobility and which constrain sustained connectivity, and test the interpretations against plausible alternatives. Preservation assessments should show why the relevant signals are attributable to the geological interval under study rather than later alteration. Independent corroboration should add distinct constraints rather than repeatedly rely on the same underlying observation.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed convincing demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: make the observations, dating uncertainties, interpretive assumptions and physical-model methods sufficiently available for independent groups to repeat the analyses and evaluate competing histories. A persuasive result would show how conclusions change when uncertain observations or model assumptions are varied, including whether the inferred transition remains supported when particular regions are excluded.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility requirement

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: completion need not mean identifying one exact onset date. A defensible interval or sequence of regional transitions could satisfy the goal if it explains how sustained global tectonics emerged and clearly distinguishes established findings from unresolved parts of the reconstruction. Evidence from a finite set of sites would establish the demonstrated geographic and temporal breadth of that account, rather than literal observation of every plate boundary or proof of uninterrupted behavior everywhere. These are proposed criteria, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based scope comparison: GEO-05, “Recovery of a detailed geological record of Earth’s first half-billion years,” is the closest overlap. Its title describes a broad early-Earth archive, whereas GEO-08 targets a specific tectonic transition and its mechanism, potentially using younger evidence as well. The full GEO-05 entry was not supplied, so its actual methods and overlap remain unverified. GEO-07, “Reconstructing the Moon-forming impact from independent geological evidence,” likewise concerns reconstruction of an ancient event, but addresses a different historical target; the supplied material does not establish a causal connection between the two.

Roster-based conceptual comparison: GEO-02, “A chemically and thermally resolved map of Earth’s deep interior,” could provide a complementary perspective on surface–interior coupling, but mapping internal structure and reconstructing tectonic onset are distinct goals. GEO-09, “Predictive laws linking erosion, sediment transport and landscape evolution,” concerns surface processes that may affect geological archives; predictive landscape laws would not independently establish when a global plate network began.

Roster-based practical comparison: GEO-01, “Reliable short-term forecasting of damaging earthquakes,” and GEO-10, “Reliable transferable forecasting of volcanic eruptions,” concern prediction of future hazards. GEO-03, “Geothermal reservoirs engineered economically in ordinary deep rock,” GEO-04, “Global-scale, verifiable mineral storage of carbon dioxide,” and GEO-06, “Discovery of globally consequential recoverable geological hydrogen,” concern energy or storage capabilities and resources. They share a broad geological setting with GEO-08, but resolving ancient tectonic onset would not by itself deliver their forecasting, engineering or resource objectives.

change_log.change: Preserved GEO-08's identity while expanding the distinction between local tectonic signals and a persistent global plate network.
change_log.reason: That distinction defines the scientific target and prevents an isolated early observation from being treated as proof of sustained global tectonics.

change_log.change: Recast the 2026 zircon interpretation as a finding reported by the supplied research that the review could not independently verify.
change_log.reason: The research reports abstract access, but the retained artifact available to the reviewer contained only a cookie challenge.

change_log.change: Preserved rock scarcity, alteration and a potentially uneven transition as research-framed concerns and hypotheses.
change_log.reason: The retained source does not substantiate these assertions, but the review did not contradict them or justify removing the concept.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to address alternative interpretations, reproducibility, uncertainty and geographic coverage.
change_log.reason: These requirements make the distinction between intermittent regional activity and sustained global tectonics assessable without demanding an exact onset date or literal universality.

change_log.change: Retained conditional geological significance and explicit limits on planetary and biological implications.
change_log.reason: The anticipated consequences are coherent assessments, but neither the achievement nor its downstream implications are demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to explain related concepts while qualifying the comparison with GEO-05.
change_log.reason: The roster supports a title-level scope comparison, but the full GEO-05 entry was unavailable to verify actual overlap.

unresolved_issues: The discrepancy between reported abstract inspection and the cookie-only retained artifact remains unresolved; the scientific content and article identity cannot be independently verified from that artifact.
The zircon study's methods, quantitative results, preservation checks and interpretation remain unavailable for assessment in the supplied review.
The supplied material does not establish whether subsequent research resolves or changes the onset question; the freshness-search record is empty.
The actual scope and methods of GEO-05 require comparison with its full entry.
The diagnostic observations and temporal coverage sufficient to distinguish sustained global connectivity from intermittent regional mobility remain to be specified and justified.
